correctness.rationale: For every finite open uniform path, positivity and the endpoint recurrence exclude any nondecaying eigenmode. The Hermitian integrated-survival observable is therefore the unique solution of \(K^\dagger T+TK=-I\). The displayed full matrix with affine even-separation real entries and odd-separation imaginary entries satisfies every diagonal, interior off-diagonal, and sink-boundary equation, giving \(\tau_{N,s}=(N+1-s)[s/\kappa+(s-1)\kappa/(4J^2)]\) for all integer \(N\ge2\), all sites \(1\le s\le N\), and positive real \(J,\kappa\). Strict convexity or AM-GM gives a unique finite optimum for \(s\ge2\); \(s=1\) has none. The standalone exact-rational verifier checks 88,560 full matrix entries for \(1\le N\le40\) at four rational parameter pairs; finite tests do not replace the universal proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Riberi Eq. (95) is an integral for semi-infinite total absorption probability, not an integrated survival first moment on a finite reflecting path; his starting-site asymptotics do not imply the finite-length formula. Varbanov Eq. (26) concerns a different measurement instrument and only its explicitly evaluated small examples share rate/inverse-rate shape. Silva Wronskians detect exceptional points but do not fix survival-time observables. A generic Lyapunov equation follows from semigroup theory, but evaluating it into the stated affine full-matrix kernel and discovering the size-free optimizer is additional nontrivial specialization.

originality.rationale: The exact finite-open-path expected absorption time and its sharp path-length-independent optimizing sink rate are absent from the materially compared quantum first-passage and non-Hermitian chain results. Closest works address a semi-infinite absorber with incomplete absorption, finite-chain spectral exceptional points without the integrated mean, a ring with dark modes, and Poisson repeated measurements with different conditional dynamics. The physical trapping study has additional radiative channels and no same formula. Dedicated equivalent-form and implied-general-theorem searches and own-ledger comparisons found no covering statement. The open risk of an unindexed explicit special-case calculation is disclosed.
residual_risks: Full-text indexing and public database searching cannot exclude an unindexed equivalent formula or an older specialized calculation.
The broad 2008 measurement framework has an algebraically related inverse-rate plus rate structure, although its explicit conditional evolution differs from terminal sink loss.
A highly specialized nearest-neighbor, no-bulk-loss limit of quantum exciton trapping literature might have been computed in an uninspected supplement.

value.rationale: The mean first absorption time is a physically natural finite-chain transport resource, and its complete all-length exact formula and size-independent sharp optimal Lindblad loss rate give a reusable design rule. The theorem pinpoints the balance between weak absorption and Zeno suppression, includes the sink-initialized exception, and extends beyond tiny numerical examples. Its limitation to coherent uniform paths is natural rather than an arbitrary sliced invariant; no unproved downstream consequence is assumed.
